questions.stem: A row over integer variables x and y reads 0.4 x + 1.5 y <= 3.35. Which row with whole numbers allows exactly the same integer points?

options.text: 4 x + 15 y <= 34, the scaled bound 33.5 rounded up
options.says: 4x + 15y is always a whole number, so it is at most 33.5 exactly when it is at most 33; 34 lets in points the row refused.

options.text: 4 x + 15 y <= 33, the scaled bound 33.5 rounded down
options.says: Right: multiply by 10, the LCM of the denominators 5 and 2, and round a <= bound down, since the left side is whole.

options.text: 0 x + 2 y <= 3, with every number rounded on its own
options.says: Rounding each coefficient changes the row; the crew row in the lesson allowed different plans after rounding.

options.text: 4 x + 15 y <= 33.5, with the scaled bound kept as it is
options.says: CP-SAT refuses a fractional bound in a row, the same way it refuses a fractional coefficient.

origin.section: Scale a Row Exactly, With a Whole-Number Multiplier

questions.stem: A developer rounds failure probabilities such as 0.31, 0.27 and 0.12 to whole numbers (scale 1) and maximizes their sum in CP-SAT. The solve returns OPTIMAL. What does the status establish?

options.text: The plan is best for the true probabilities as well as the rounded ones
options.says: The lesson's run at scale 1 was OPTIMAL and avoided five fewer failures than the best plan.

options.text: The rounding was checked by CP-SAT and found to be enough
options.says: CP-SAT solves the coefficients it is given; it cannot know what they were rounded from.

options.text: The plan is best for the rounded numbers, not the true ones
options.says: Right: the status is about the model as given, and rounding to whole numbers changed which plans look best.

options.text: The sums overflowed, so the plan came from a partial search
options.says: An overflow risk makes the model MODEL_INVALID before any search; these numbers are tiny.

origin.section: Scale an Objective Enough to Keep Its Order

questions.stem: A developer sets `enumerate_all_solutions = True` on a model that still has its `maximize` objective, and collects each reported plan in a solution callback. Several plans tie for the best value. What does the collected list hold?

options.text: only the improving plans, which can miss tied best plans
options.says: Right: with the objective on, the run in the lesson reported 2 solutions while 9 plans tied for the best score.

options.text: every tied best plan, each one reported exactly once by the solver
options.says: That needs the second solve, with the objective fixed at its best value and then removed.

options.text: every feasible plan of the model, the tied best ones among them
options.says: With an objective the solver reports improving solutions, not every feasible one.

options.text: no plan at all, since the solver refuses the parameter there
options.says: The solve runs and reports solutions; the parameter is simply meant for models without an objective.

origin.section: Every Optimal Plan: Optimize, Fix the Objective, Enumerate
